title: Data sorter
instruction: Structured data (a fixed order) or unstructured data (no order)?

items.text: A table of marks in the school system
items.why: Each row is a pupil, each column a subject or a date.
A picture has no rows and columns of data. Someone has to recognise what's in it.
A fixed table: stop, time, route.

items.text: A voice message from a friend
items.why: Sound with no fixed order. You have to listen to find out what's in it.

items.text: An online shop's stock (rows and columns)
items.why: Every product has the same details: name, price, number in stock.
Picture and sound without a table. Only the details around it are fixed, such as the number of likes.
Each row has the same fields: player and score. It can be sorted.
Free text. Everyone writes it differently.

debrief: Structured data has fixed rows and columns, so you can search and sort it. A photo, a voice message or an essay carry information too, just without a fixed order.
